content.user_title: Draft Clear Commit Messages from Staged Changes
content.value_statement: Staged changes can be difficult to summarize accurately. This skill reviews the diff and drafts a clear commit message with optional context and file counts.
actual_capabilities: Reviews staged changes through git diff --cached.
Identifies common change types, including features, fixes, documentation, and refactoring.
Drafts descriptive or conventional commit messages.
Adjusts message style, detail, context, and file counts through configuration.
Shows a draft for the user to review and copy before committing.
limitations: It only analyzes changes that are already staged.
It infers intent from a diff and may need clarification for ambiguous changes.
It does not stage files, modify the repository, or create commits.
Message quality depends on the completeness of the staged changes and diff context.

use_cases.title: Prepare a feature commit
use_cases.description: Turn staged implementation, tests, and documentation into a message that explains the feature and its purpose.

use_cases.title: Standardize team history
use_cases.description: Use conventional formatting to create consistent commit messages for a shared repository.

use_cases.title: Document maintenance work
use_cases.description: Summarize refactoring or configuration changes with useful context for later reviewers.

prompt_templates.title: Draft my first commit message
prompt_templates.prompt: Review my staged changes and draft a concise commit message.

prompt_templates.title: Explain the change
prompt_templates.prompt: Analyze my staged diff and draft a message that states what changed and why it matters.

prompt_templates.title: Use Conventional Commits
prompt_templates.prompt: Review my staged changes and draft a Conventional Commit message with a short explanatory body.

prompt_templates.title: Create a detailed release-ready message
prompt_templates.prompt: Analyze the staged diff. Draft a detailed commit message with scope, impact, and file counts. Ask a question if the intent is unclear.

output_examples.input: Staged changes add validation tests and update the API handler.
output_examples.output:
fix: validate API request input

Rejects invalid requests before they reach the handler and adds coverage for the new validation paths.

output_examples.input: Staged changes add setup instructions and link them from the README.
output_examples.output:
Document local setup process

Adds a setup guide and links it from the README so new contributors can start work more quickly.

best_practices: Stage only related changes before requesting a draft.
Review the generated message against the diff before using it.
Use the configuration to match your repository commit convention.
anti_patterns: Do not use a draft without reviewing whether it describes the staged changes.
Do not stage unrelated work together and expect one accurate message.
Do not rely on inferred intent when important business context is missing.

faq.question: Does this skill create a commit?
faq.answer: No. It drafts a message for you to review and use yourself.

faq.question: Which changes does it analyze?
faq.answer: It analyzes staged changes using git diff --cached.

faq.question: Can I use Conventional Commits?
faq.answer: Yes. Set the format option to conventional in the skill configuration.

faq.question: Can I edit the drafted message?
faq.answer: Yes. The message is a draft that you can revise before committing.

faq.question: What happens when no changes are staged?
faq.answer: The skill reports that no staged changes are available and suggests staging changes first.

faq.question: Can the skill include more detail?
faq.answer: Yes. Configure the message length, context, and file-count options for a more detailed draft.
